decision.query: OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND ("central corneal thickness") AND ("optical coherence tomography") AND ("ultrasound pachymetry") AND (healthy OR normal)
decision.reason: Find open-access paired primary studies in normal adult eyes reporting OCT and contact ultrasound central corneal thickness, preferably with agreement statistics needed to model within-eye differences.

decision.query: OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND FIRST_PDATE:[2005-01-01 TO 2020-12-31] AND TITLE_ABS:("corneal thickness") AND TITLE_ABS:("optical coherence tomography") AND TITLE_ABS:(ultrasound) AND (agreement OR "Bland-Altman")
decision.reason: Find paired method-comparison studies with agreement statistics that permit modeling same-eye differences, while restricting the search to established publications.

Read this prospective paired comparison to verify adult unoperated-eye eligibility, contact ultrasound and anterior-segment OCT protocols, and quantitative agreement statistics suitable for generating same-eye measurements and estimating differences exceeding 20 micrometres.

Check this paired healthy-eye study for explicit adult eligibility and internally consistent OCT–contact ultrasound agreement statistics. The previously opened study has conflicting mean-difference, SD, and limits-of-agreement values, making its estimated percentage above 20 micrometres unreliable.

Check this large adult paired AS-OCT–ultrasound study for explicit exclusion of operated or diseased corneas and usable marginal thickness and within-eye agreement statistics. The opened studies have either internally inconsistent agreement values or missing numerical tables, limiting defensible virtual-cohort calibration.

This paired primary study examined 50 unoperated eyes of 30 healthy volunteers (mean age 27.0±2.9 years), excluding corneal pathology, and measured central corneal thickness using Visante anterior-segment OCT and contact ultrasound. For this clearly defined population, the text reports OCT-minus-ultrasound bias of −3.6 µm and a most extreme 95% agreement limit of −14.9 µm, permitting an approximate paired-difference SD of (14.9−3.6)/1.96 under the stated Bland–Altman model. These support a model-based virtual cohort and estimation of the proportion with |difference|>20 µm. Explain the normal-tail assumption, distinguish corrected agreement variability from triplicate-average variability, and disclose that marginal thickness tables and an explicit age range are unavailable in the retrieved text.
